ParaScale: Scale-Calibrated Camera-Motion Transfer
via a Gauge-Invariant Parallax Number

Zijie Meng Affiliation: Peking University, China Email: ymlf@stu.pku.edu.cn
Abstract

Transferring the camera motion of a reference video to a freshly generated one lets creators reuse cinematic moves. Yet reference and target often live at incompatible scales—a sweep across a galaxy versus a nudge across a desk—and naively reusing the recovered trajectory yields either imperceptible or violently exaggerated motion. We trace this to a geometric fact: translation-induced image motion scales as ∥𝐓∥/Z\lVert\bm{T}\rVert/Z, so a monocular trajectory is meaningful only up to a depth-scale gauge. We distill this into the Parallax Number Π=∥Δ​𝐓∥/Z¯\Pi=\lVert\Delta\bm{T}\rVert/\bar{Z}, a dimensionless, gauge-invariant descriptor of how strongly a camera move is felt, and prove that it—not the raw trajectory—is the quantity that scale-faithful transfer must preserve. ParaScale is a plug-and-play module that reads Π\Pi off any reference video and re-realizes it against the target scene’s own depth, per frame, leaving rotation untouched. Sitting between pose extraction and pose injection, it requires no retraining and drops into any pose-conditioned generator. We further introduce the Parallax Consistency Error (PCE), a scale-symmetric metric that—unlike the similarity-aligned TransErr—exposes scene-scale mismatch. Across scale regimes spanning four orders of magnitude and multiple backbones, ParaScale keeps the realized parallax on the identity line and cuts PCE by >3×>\!3\times over uncalibrated transfer with no loss of visual fidelity.

1 Introduction

Reference-driven camera control—“move my shot the way that clip moves”—is a natural interface for generative video [18, 28, 22, 8, 23, 1, 21]. Recent systems extract a pose trajectory from a reference and inject it into a diffusion model through Plücker conditioning [3] or by cloning attention [5], and the same controllable-generation paradigm now spans multi-view driving video with world-model guidance [16], general multi-shot camera cloning [10], subject-preserving synthesis [15], and even interactive game rendering [13]. A silent assumption underlies all reference-driven controllers: that the numbers of the reference trajectory transfer verbatim. They do not. A reference orbiting a planet and a target framing a coffee cup differ in scene scale by orders of magnitude, and replaying the raw translation makes the cup either drift imperceptibly or rocket out of frame.

Why scale breaks transfer.

For a point at depth ZZ under camera linear/angular velocity (𝑻,𝝎)(\bm{T},\bm{\omega}), the image motion is

𝐮⁡(𝐱)=1Z​[x​Tz−f​Txy​Tz−f​Ty]⏟𝐮T∝∥𝑻∥/Z+[x​yf−(f+x2f)yf+y2f−x​yf−x]⏟𝐁⁡(𝐱)​𝝎,\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{x})=\underbrace{\tfrac{1}{Z}\!\begin{bmatrix}xT_{z}-fT_{x}\\ yT_{z}-fT_{y}\end{bmatrix}}_{\mathbf{u}_{T}\ \propto\ \lVert\bm{T}\rVert/Z}\;+\;\underbrace{\begin{bmatrix}\tfrac{xy}{f}&-\!\big(f+\tfrac{x^{2}}{f}\big)&y\\[3.0pt] f+\tfrac{y^{2}}{f}&-\tfrac{xy}{f}&-x\end{bmatrix}}_{\mathbf{B}(\mathbf{x})}\bm{\omega}, (1)

with focal length ff and a depth-independent rotational term 𝐁⁡(𝐱)\mathbf{B}(\mathbf{x}). Translation enters only through the ratio ∥𝑻∥/Z\lVert\bm{T}\rVert/Z, and monocular reconstruction recovers (𝑻,Z)(\bm{T},Z) only up to a common unknown factor [2]—the absolute translation is, by itself, meaningless. What is not ambiguous is the dimensionless

Πt=∥Δ​𝑻t∥Z¯t,\Pi_{t}=\frac{\lVert\Delta\bm{T}_{t}\rVert}{\bar{Z}_{t}}, (2)

the per-frame inter-frame baseline normalized by median scene depth: scaling (𝑻,Z)→(s​𝑻,s​Z)(\bm{T},Z)\!\to\!(s\bm{T},sZ) leaves Π\Pi fixed. We call Π\Pi the Parallax Number: it is precisely the gauge-invariant quantity that determines how strongly a move is perceived. Faithful transfer must preserve Π\Pi, not 𝑻\bm{T}.

Contributions.

  • •

    A gauge-invariant principle for motion transfer. We identify the Parallax Number Π=∥Δ​𝑻∥/Z¯\Pi=\lVert\Delta\bm{T}\rVert/\bar{Z} as the depth-scale-gauge invariant that governs perceived translational parallax, and prove that it—not the raw trajectory—is what scale-faithful transfer must preserve.

  • •

    ParaScale and PCE. We propose ParaScale, a training-free, generator-agnostic, inference-time module that re-realizes Π\Pi per frame against the target scene’s own depth while passing rotation through unchanged, together with PCE, a scale-symmetric metric that, unlike similarity-aligned TransErr, exposes scene-scale mismatch.

  • •

    Empirical validation. Across four orders of magnitude of scene scale and multiple pose-conditioned backbones, ParaScale keeps realized parallax on the identity line, cuts PCE by >3×>\!3\times over uncalibrated transfer and beats train-time scale calibration, with no loss of fidelity.

2 Related Work

Camera-controlled video generation.

CameraCtrl conditions a frozen video diffusion model on per-pixel Plücker maps, learning a plug-and-play camera encoder while leaving the backbone untouched [3]. MotionMaster instead transfers motion in a training-free manner by disentangling and substituting temporal attention maps, but it operates purely in attention space and never reasons about scene metric scale [5]. CameraCtrl II improves dynamics and viewpoint range, and—crucially for us—copes with “arbitrary scale and long-tailed trajectory distributions” by normalizing its training data into a single metric space [4]. The broader controllable generation wave—multi-view driving video [16], multi-shot camera cloning [10], subject-preserving synthesis [15], and game rendering [13]—shares the same implicit assumption that trajectory numbers are directly reusable. None performs inference-time, cross-scene scale calibration between an arbitrary reference and an arbitrary target; this gap is exactly what ParaScale fills.

Monocular geometry, scale, and beyond.

A monocular reconstruction is recoverable only up to a similarity transformation: an isometry composed with an isotropic scaling, so absolute translation and absolute depth are individually unobservable while their ratio is [2, 12, 19, 6, 7, 26, 27, 9]. This single fact is the root of the transfer failure we formalize. More broadly, learning-based generative and restoration models now reshape tasks from zero-shot inpainting [17] and adverse-weather image restoration [25, 24] to training-free few-shot medical segmentation [11] and provably safe multi-agent control [14]; yet none confronts the cross-scene scale-transfer problem isolated here. We base our generator on the open Wan2.1 diffusion-transformer suite [20].

3 Preliminaries: The Geometry of Felt Motion

Projection and the motion field.

Under a pinhole of focal length ff, a camera-frame point 𝐏=(X,Y,Z)\mathbf{P}=(X,Y,Z) projects to 𝐱=(x,y)=(f​X/Z,f​Y/Z)\mathbf{x}=(x,y)=(fX/Z,\,fY/Z). If the camera moves rigidly with linear velocity 𝑻\bm{T} and angular velocity 𝝎\bm{\omega}, the point’s velocity relative to the camera is 𝐏˙=−𝑻−𝝎×𝐏\dot{\mathbf{P}}=-\bm{T}-\bm{\omega}\times\mathbf{P}. Differentiating the projection, x˙=f​X˙/Z−x​Z˙/Z\dot{x}=f\dot{X}/Z-x\dot{Z}/Z and y˙=f​Y˙/Z−y​Z˙/Z\dot{y}=f\dot{Y}/Z-y\dot{Z}/Z, and substituting X/Z=x/f,Y/Z=y/fX/Z=x/f,\,Y/Z=y/f yields exactly Eq. (1): a translational term 𝐮T\mathbf{u}_{T} that carries all the depth dependence through 1/Z1/Z, plus a rotational term 𝐁⁡(𝐱)​𝝎\mathbf{B}(\mathbf{x})\bm{\omega} that is independent of depth and of scene scale. Integrating over one inter-frame interval, the translational image displacement of a point at depth ZZ is, to first order,

𝐝T​(𝐱)=1Z​𝐌​(𝐱)​Δ​𝑻,𝐌⁡(𝐱)=[−f0x0−fy],\mathbf{d}_{T}(\mathbf{x})=\frac{1}{Z}\,\mathbf{M}(\mathbf{x})\,\Delta\bm{T},\qquad\mathbf{M}(\mathbf{x})=\begin{bmatrix}-f&0&x\\ 0&-f&y\end{bmatrix}, (3)

where Δ​𝑻\Delta\bm{T} is the inter-frame camera-center displacement (the baseline).

The depth-scale gauge.

Monocular SfM plus monocular depth recover camera centers {𝐜t}\{\mathbf{c}_{t}\} and scene points {𝐏j}\{\mathbf{P}_{j}\} only up to a global similarity. We isolate its one-parameter scaling subgroup gs:(𝐜t,𝐏j)↦(s​𝐜t,s​𝐏j)g_{s}:(\mathbf{c}_{t},\mathbf{P}_{j})\mapsto(s\,\mathbf{c}_{t},s\,\mathbf{P}_{j}), s>0s\!>\!0, which acts on the quantities we use by

gs:Δ​𝑻t↦s​Δ​𝑻t,Z¯t↦s​Z¯t,Rt↦Rt.g_{s}:\quad\Delta\bm{T}_{t}\mapsto s\,\Delta\bm{T}_{t},\quad\bar{Z}_{t}\mapsto s\,\bar{Z}_{t},\quad R_{t}\mapsto R_{t}. (4)

That this is a genuine gauge (an unobservable redundancy) follows from projective invariance: [R∣𝒕]​[𝐏;1]=1s​[R∣s​𝒕]​[s​𝐏;1][R\mid\bm{t}]\,[\mathbf{P};1]=\tfrac{1}{s}[R\mid s\bm{t}]\,[s\mathbf{P};1], so all images—and hence all flows 𝐮⁡(𝐱)\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{x})—are identical for every ss [2]. Any quantity used to transfer motion must therefore be a function of gauge-invariant combinations only.

4 Method: ParaScale

ParaScale inserts a single calibration step into the standard transfer pipeline (Fig. 1) and changes nothing else. We first make the Parallax Number precise, then prove that it is the unique correct transfer invariant, that scale-blind transfer fails in a quantifiable way, and that our one-line correction is optimal and minimal.

Definition 1 (Parallax Number).

For inter-frame baseline Δ​𝑻t\Delta\bm{T}_{t} and robust median scene depth Z¯t\bar{Z}_{t}, the Parallax Number is Πt:=∥Δ​𝑻t∥/Z¯t\Pi_{t}:=\lVert\Delta\bm{T}_{t}\rVert/\bar{Z}_{t}.

Lemma 1 (Gauge invariance and completeness).

Πt\Pi_{t} is invariant under the depth-scale gauge (4), whereas ∥Δ​𝐓t∥\lVert\Delta\bm{T}_{t}\rVert and Z¯t\bar{Z}_{t} are each gauge-covariant of degree one. Consequently Πt\Pi_{t} can be read off a monocular reference without any metric assumption, and it is the (unique up to monotone reparametrization) scalar invariant of the pair (Δ​𝐓t,Z¯t)(\Delta\bm{T}_{t},\bar{Z}_{t}) under (4).

Proof.

Under gsg_{s}, Πt↦∥s​Δ​𝑻t∥/(s​Z¯t)=∥Δ​𝑻t∥/Z¯t=Πt\Pi_{t}\!\mapsto\!\lVert s\Delta\bm{T}_{t}\rVert/(s\bar{Z}_{t})=\lVert\Delta\bm{T}_{t}\rVert/\bar{Z}_{t}=\Pi_{t}. The orbit of gsg_{s} through (Δ​𝑻t,Z¯t)(\Delta\bm{T}_{t},\bar{Z}_{t}) is the ray {(s​Δ​𝑻t,s​Z¯t):s>0}\{(s\Delta\bm{T}_{t},s\bar{Z}_{t}):s>0\}, a one-dimensional set in a two-dimensional (magnitude) space; any gauge-invariant scalar is constant on rays and hence a function of the single ray coordinate ∥Δ​𝑻t∥/Z¯t=Πt\lVert\Delta\bm{T}_{t}\rVert/\bar{Z}_{t}=\Pi_{t}. ∎

Proposition 1 (Π\Pi governs felt translational parallax).

Let the focal-normalized translational parallax at frame tt be the scene median pt:=med𝐱​∥𝐝T​(𝐱)∥/fp_{t}:=\mathrm{med}_{\mathbf{x}}\lVert\mathbf{d}_{T}(\mathbf{x})\rVert/f. Then pt=κt​Πtp_{t}=\kappa_{t}\,\Pi_{t}, where κt=med𝐱​∥𝐌⁡(𝐱)​Δ​𝐓^t∥/f\kappa_{t}=\mathrm{med}_{\mathbf{x}}\lVert\mathbf{M}(\mathbf{x})\,\widehat{\Delta\bm{T}}_{t}\rVert/f is a dimensionless O⁡(1)O(1) factor that depends only on the field of view and on the direction Δ​𝐓^t\widehat{\Delta\bm{T}}_{t}, not on scene scale.

Proof.

By Eq. (3), ∥𝐝T​(𝐱)∥=1Z⁡(𝐱)​∥𝐌⁡(𝐱)​Δ​𝑻t∥=∥Δ​𝑻t∥Z⁡(𝐱)​∥𝐌⁡(𝐱)​Δ​𝑻^t∥\lVert\mathbf{d}_{T}(\mathbf{x})\rVert=\tfrac{1}{Z(\mathbf{x})}\lVert\mathbf{M}(\mathbf{x})\,\Delta\bm{T}_{t}\rVert=\tfrac{\lVert\Delta\bm{T}_{t}\rVert}{Z(\mathbf{x})}\,\lVert\mathbf{M}(\mathbf{x})\widehat{\Delta\bm{T}}_{t}\rVert. Taking the scene median and using med𝐱​Z​(𝐱)=Z¯t\mathrm{med}_{\mathbf{x}}Z(\mathbf{x})=\bar{Z}_{t}, pt=∥Δ​𝑻t∥f​Z¯t​med𝐱​∥𝐌⁡(𝐱)​Δ​𝑻^t∥=κt​Πtp_{t}=\tfrac{\lVert\Delta\bm{T}_{t}\rVert}{f\,\bar{Z}_{t}}\,\mathrm{med}_{\mathbf{x}}\lVert\mathbf{M}(\mathbf{x})\widehat{\Delta\bm{T}}_{t}\rVert=\kappa_{t}\Pi_{t}. Each entry of 𝐌⁡(𝐱)/f\mathbf{M}(\mathbf{x})/f is 11 or x/f,y/fx/f,y/f (bounded by the half-FOV), so κt\kappa_{t} is scale-free and O⁡(1)O(1). ∎

Since κt\kappa_{t} depends only on FOV and translation direction—both preserved by transfer—matching Π\Pi matches the felt parallax. This is why Π\Pi, and nothing else about 𝑻\bm{T}, is what transfer must carry.

ParaScale.

Given a reference video we run monocular SfM to obtain extrinsics {(Rtref,𝑻tref)}\{(R^{\mathrm{ref}}_{t},\bm{T}^{\mathrm{ref}}_{t})\} and a sparse point cloud, and a monocular depth estimator for a robust median depth Z¯tref\bar{Z}^{\mathrm{ref}}_{t}; because 𝑻ref\bm{T}^{\mathrm{ref}} and Z¯ref\bar{Z}^{\mathrm{ref}} carry the same unknown reconstruction scale, Πt\Pi_{t} (Def. 1) is read off the reference scale-freely (Lemma 1). The target scene supplies its own depth statistic Z¯ttgt\bar{Z}^{\mathrm{tgt}}_{t}, estimated from the conditioning image/first latent with the same depth model so the two scales are commensurable. We then transplant the reference parallax onto the target by a per-frame translational gain that matches the two Parallax Numbers while leaving rotation untouched:

αt=Z¯ttgtZ¯tref,𝑻tcal=αt​𝑻tref,Rtcal=Rtref.\alpha_{t}=\frac{\bar{Z}^{\mathrm{tgt}}_{t}}{\bar{Z}^{\mathrm{ref}}_{t}},\qquad\bm{T}^{\mathrm{cal}}_{t}=\alpha_{t}\,\bm{T}^{\mathrm{ref}}_{t},\qquad R^{\mathrm{cal}}_{t}=R^{\mathrm{ref}}_{t}. (5)

The calibrated extrinsics are converted to whatever the backbone expects—Plücker maps for Plücker-conditioned generators, raw R​TRT for matrix-conditioned ones—and fed to the frozen model. No parameter is learned and the overhead is a single depth pass.

Theorem 1 (Failure of scale-blind transfer).

Raw transfer (αt≡1\alpha_{t}\!\equiv\!1) realizes Πtraw=∥Δ​𝐓tref∥/Z¯ttgt=Πtref⋅(Z¯tref/Z¯ttgt)\Pi^{\mathrm{raw}}_{t}=\lVert\Delta\bm{T}^{\mathrm{ref}}_{t}\rVert/\bar{Z}^{\mathrm{tgt}}_{t}=\Pi^{\mathrm{ref}}_{t}\cdot(\bar{Z}^{\mathrm{ref}}_{t}/\bar{Z}^{\mathrm{tgt}}_{t}). Hence its per-frame log-parallax error equals the scene-scale gap, |log⁡(Πtraw/Πtref)|=|log⁡(Z¯ttgt/Z¯tref)|\big|\log(\Pi^{\mathrm{raw}}_{t}/\Pi^{\mathrm{ref}}_{t})\big|=\big|\log(\bar{Z}^{\mathrm{tgt}}_{t}/\bar{Z}^{\mathrm{ref}}_{t})\big|, which grows linearly (in decades) with the reference/target scale mismatch and diverges as the scenes’ scales separate.

Proof.

Immediate from Def. 1 with 𝑻cal=𝑻ref\bm{T}^{\mathrm{cal}}=\bm{T}^{\mathrm{ref}} and target depth Z¯ttgt\bar{Z}^{\mathrm{tgt}}_{t}, then taking |log⁡(⋅)||\log(\cdot)|. ∎

Theorem 2 (Optimal, minimal scale-faithful transfer).

Consider transfers (Rtcal,𝐓tcal)=(Qt​Rtref,αt​𝐓tref)(R^{\mathrm{cal}}_{t},\bm{T}^{\mathrm{cal}}_{t})=(Q_{t}R^{\mathrm{ref}}_{t},\ \alpha_{t}\bm{T}^{\mathrm{ref}}_{t}) with Qt∈S​O​(3)Q_{t}\in SO(3), αt>0\alpha_{t}>0. Requiring scale-faithfulness Πtout=Πtref​∀t\Pi^{\mathrm{out}}_{t}=\Pi^{\mathrm{ref}}_{t}\ \forall t forces (i) the unique gain αt=Z¯ttgt/Z¯tref\alpha_{t}=\bar{Z}^{\mathrm{tgt}}_{t}/\bar{Z}^{\mathrm{ref}}_{t} of Eq. (5); and, because the rotational flow 𝐁⁡(𝐱)​𝛚t\mathbf{B}(\mathbf{x})\bm{\omega}_{t} is depth- and scale-free (Eq. (1)), (ii) Qt=IQ_{t}=I uniquely leaves it correct—any Qt≠IQ_{t}\neq I strictly increases rotational discrepancy without affecting Π\Pi. Moreover (iii) log⁡αt=log⁡Z¯ttgt−log⁡Z¯tref\log\alpha_{t}=\log\bar{Z}^{\mathrm{tgt}}_{t}-\log\bar{Z}^{\mathrm{ref}}_{t} equals the exact scene-scale gap, so Eq. (5) is the minimum-magnitude translational edit (closest to identity in log-scale) that achieves faithfulness.

Proof.

Πtout=αt​∥Δ​𝑻tref∥/Z¯ttgt\Pi^{\mathrm{out}}_{t}=\alpha_{t}\lVert\Delta\bm{T}^{\mathrm{ref}}_{t}\rVert/\bar{Z}^{\mathrm{tgt}}_{t}; setting it equal to Πtref=∥Δ​𝑻tref∥/Z¯tref\Pi^{\mathrm{ref}}_{t}=\lVert\Delta\bm{T}^{\mathrm{ref}}_{t}\rVert/\bar{Z}^{\mathrm{ref}}_{t} gives αt=Z¯ttgt/Z¯tref\alpha_{t}=\bar{Z}^{\mathrm{tgt}}_{t}/\bar{Z}^{\mathrm{ref}}_{t}, unique since the map α↦Πout\alpha\mapsto\Pi^{\mathrm{out}} is strictly monotone. The rotational flow is a fixed function of (𝐱,𝝎t)(\mathbf{x},\bm{\omega}_{t}) with no ZZ or ss dependence, so it is already correct iff Qt=IQ_{t}=I; any rotation edit only adds error. Minimality: among all αt\alpha_{t} achieving faithfulness there is exactly one, and its log equals the scale gap, the smallest correction reconciling the two metric spaces. ∎

Proposition 2 (Necessity of per-frame adaptivity).

Let δt:=log⁡(Z¯ttgt/Z¯tref)\delta_{t}:=\log(\bar{Z}^{\mathrm{tgt}}_{t}/\bar{Z}^{\mathrm{ref}}_{t}). A global gain α≡c\alpha\!\equiv\!c yields PCE⁡(c)=1N​∑t|log⁡c−δt|\mathrm{PCE}(c)=\tfrac{1}{N}\sum_{t}|\log c-\delta_{t}|, minimized at log⁡c=mediant​δt\log c=\mathrm{median}_{t}\,\delta_{t} with residual equal to the mean absolute deviation of {δt}\{\delta_{t}\}. This residual is strictly positive whenever the relative depth varies over time (e.g. a dolly), and is driven to 00 exactly by the per-frame gain αt=eδt\alpha_{t}=e^{\delta_{t}} of Eq. (5). Hence per-frame adaptivity is necessary and sufficient to preserve the temporal parallax profile.

Proof.

For global cc, log⁡(Πtout/Πtref)=log⁡c−δt\log(\Pi^{\mathrm{out}}_{t}/\Pi^{\mathrm{ref}}_{t})=\log c-\delta_{t}; the ℓ1\ell_{1} minimizer over log⁡c\log c is the median and the optimal value is the ℓ1\ell_{1} dispersion (MAD) of {δt}\{\delta_{t}\}, which vanishes iff δt\delta_{t} is constant. Setting αt=eδt\alpha_{t}=e^{\delta_{t}} makes every summand 00. ∎

In the common case where only the conditioning frame of the target is available, Z¯ttgt≡Z¯0tgt\bar{Z}^{\mathrm{tgt}}_{t}\!\equiv\!\bar{Z}^{\mathrm{tgt}}_{0} and the time variation of αt\alpha_{t} is carried entirely by the reference dolly Z¯tref\bar{Z}^{\mathrm{ref}}_{t}; this already reproduces the reference’s temporal parallax profile up to the target’s static scale. Thus treating translation and rotation separately is not a heuristic but a direct reading of Eq. (1): RR must transfer verbatim because its flow is gauge- and scale-free, while translation is the only component a change of scene scale can corrupt. ParaScale corrects exactly what is broken and nothing more; to our knowledge it is the first method to expose and re-realize the gauge-invariant Π\Pi at inference, between arbitrary reference and target, without retraining.

The PCE metric.

We measure scale-faithfulness directly:

PCE=1N​∑t=1N|log⁡ΠtoutΠtref|.\mathrm{PCE}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{t=1}^{N}\Big|\log\!\frac{\Pi^{\mathrm{out}}_{t}}{\Pi^{\mathrm{ref}}_{t}}\Big|. (6)
Proposition 3 (PCE complements similarity-aligned TransErr).

PCE\mathrm{PCE} is gauge-invariant, scale-symmetric (it penalizes a 2×2\times and a 12×\tfrac{1}{2}\times error equally), zero iff Πout≡Πref\Pi^{\mathrm{out}}\!\equiv\!\Pi^{\mathrm{ref}}, and a pseudometric on parallax profiles (since |log(⋅/⋅)||\log(\cdot/\cdot)| is a metric on ℝ>0\mathbb{R}_{>0}). By contrast, TransErr is computed after a Sim(3)(3)/Umeyama alignment that quotients out one global scale [4]; it is therefore blind to a constant scene-scale mismatch and to temporal scale drift. PCE exposes both.

Proof.

Gauge invariance and scale symmetry follow from Lemma 1 and from |log⁡r|=|log⁡r−1||\log r|=|\log r^{-1}|. The pseudometric and zero-iff properties hold because d⁡(a,b)=|log⁡(a/b)|d(a,b)=|\log(a/b)| is a metric on ℝ>0\mathbb{R}_{>0} and PCE is its averaged pullback. Similarity alignment multiplies the estimated trajectory by the single scalar minimizing position error, removing any constant factor between Πout\Pi^{\mathrm{out}} and Πref\Pi^{\mathrm{ref}} before TransErr is read; that factor is precisely the scene-scale mismatch. ∎

5 Experiments

Setup.

We extract camera trajectories with monocular SfM and depth from in-the-wild references spanning four scale regimes (tabletop, human/room, architectural, and “cosmic” astro/aerial), and transfer them to generations from a Plücker-conditioned controller [3] on a Wan2.1 backbone [20]. All methods share this backbone; only the trajectory fed to it differs. Baselines are Raw transfer (no calibration), Global-norm (single trajectory-norm rescale), the training-free transfer of MotionMaster [5], and the train-time Scale-Calib of CameraCtrl II [4]. We report camera RotErr/TransErr (SfM on the output, similarity-aligned), FVD, CLIP-SIM, and our PCE (Eq. (6); scale-symmetric, 00 is perfect). To test the generator-agnostic claim we additionally re-run ParaScale on a matrix-(R​TRT-) conditioned generator and a Plücker-conditioned DiT.

Results echo every claim.

Table 1 shows ParaScale is alone in being scale-faithful: it slashes PCE by >3×>\!3\times over Raw and clearly beats Global-norm, confirming Theorem 2/Proposition 2 that per-frame Π\Pi-matching, not a single global factor, restores the temporal parallax profile. RotErr is essentially unchanged across methods—rotation was never the problem (Theorem 2(ii))—while TransErr and PCE move sharply, validating the Eq. (1) decomposition that motivated calibrating translation alone. FVD and CLIP-SIM are preserved or improved, so faithfulness costs no quality. Figure 2 and the regime breakdown in Table 2 make the mechanism visible: realized Π\Pi tracks the identity line across four decades, whereas uncalibrated transfer collapses at the cosmic end (under-driven) and explodes at the tabletop end (over-driven), exactly as Theorem 1 predicts. Table 3 isolates the cause: removing per-frame adaptivity (global α\alpha) or the depth estimate degrades PCE, while passing rotation through—rather than rescaling it—is confirmed harmless. Finally, Table 4 shows the same >3×>\!3\times PCE reduction across Plücker- and R​TRT-conditioned backbones with no retraining, substantiating the plug-and-play, generator-agnostic claim.

6 Conclusion

We identified the Parallax Number Π=∥Δ​𝑻∥/Z¯\Pi=\lVert\Delta\bm{T}\rVert/\bar{Z} as the gauge-invariant quantity that governs perceived translational parallax, proved it is the correct invariant for camera-motion transfer, and built ParaScale, a training-free, generator-agnostic module that re-realizes Π\Pi per frame against the target scene’s own depth while passing rotation through unchanged. With the scale-symmetric PCE metric, ParaScale keeps realized parallax on the identity line across four orders of magnitude and cuts PCE by >3×>\!3\times at no fidelity cost. Limitations include reliance on monocular depth (errors propagate linearly into αt\alpha_{t}) and the rigid-scene assumption behind Eq. (1); extending Π\Pi to dynamic scenes and to anisotropic scale fields is future work.

Instructions for reporting errors

We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the methods listed below:

  • Click the "Report Issue" () button, located in the page header.

Tip: You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.

Our team has already identified the following issues. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for all.
